summary: This Dockerfile sets up a Node.js environment running Docusaurus, a documentation site generator. It installs Docusaurus in the /app directory, switches to a non-root user for security, installs dependencies, copies the project files, and starts the development server listening on all network interfaces.

explanations.3: create-docusaurus generates a new Docusaurus project in /app using the 'classic' template with JavaScript. The backslash continues the command on the next line.
explanations.4: chown changes ownership of all files in /app to the 'node' user and group so the non-root user can access them.
explanations.6: USER node switches from the default root user to 'node', a less-privileged user, for better security when running containers.
explanations.10: yarn install downloads and installs all the project dependencies defined in package.json into node_modules.
explanations.12: COPY . . copies all files from your local project directory into the /app directory inside the container.
explanations.14: CMD sets the default command to run when the container starts. The --host 0.0.0.0 makes the server accessible from outside the container, not just localhost.
